name: Lecah
overview: Lecah is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified in Scripture as the son of Er. His mention is brief and specific, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. His identity is primarily grounded in his lineage within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Lecah means "to you" in Hebrew. It is a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:21. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God or carries a special title beyond its literal meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Lecah as the son of Er, establishing his immediate paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Lecah's significance lies chiefly in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, connecting him to the broader narrative of Israel's tribal history. His mention in 1 Chronicles serves to preserve the lineage and heritage of Judah's descendants, which is foundational to understanding the tribe's role in God's redemptive plan.
